text:
The closed-loop gain should be about -Rf/R1 = -1059.2/758061 ≈ -1.40e-3, which is inside the target window. The simulated -6.4e-4 is roughly half that. The Rf and R1 sensitivities confirm the ideal ratio, so the shortfall comes from low open-loop gain rather than a resistor value. The op-amp's loop gain is too low for the feedback network to hold the ideal ratio.

The tail device M5 is the most likely cause. It is in triode (Vds = 0.217 V, Vdsat = 0.546 V). Its drain sits at the diff-pair source, which is set by the 0.9 V common-mode input minus about 0.68 V of Vgs, so M5 cannot reach saturation at this bias. The tail current is 26 µA, while the mirror ratio M5/M6 = 2.02/0.49 ≈ 4.1 would predict about 41 µA. M5 is oversized relative to the reference mirror, so it demands more current than the headroom allows. Triode operation collapses the tail's output resistance and the first-stage gm, which cuts open-loop gain and therefore the closed-loop gain.

The other specs are fine: bandwidth is 447 MHz, power is 130 µW (72 µA total), and the offset is -25 mV. This fits a fault confined to the tail mirror device rather than the feedback network.

M5 is pushed into triode (Vds=0.217 V < Vdsat=0.546 V). This collapses the tail output resistance and first-stage gm, reducing open-loop gain so the closed-loop gain is about half of -Rf/R1 (-6.4e-4 vs. the -1.4e-3 target). Fix: reduce M5 width (or the M5/M6 ratio) so M5 saturates at the ~0.9 V common-mode bias."}
